prompt: According to the lesson, which statement describes intelligence?
options: The interception of signals, whether communications between people or electronic emissions, by Army units in the field
Any information gathered about foreign nations or operating areas, whether or not it has been evaluated
The product of collecting, evaluating, analyzing and integrating all information significant to military planning
The equipment and sensors used to gather information in the area of operations
explanation: Slide 12 defines intelligence as a product that results from collection, evaluation, analysis and integration. Raw or unevaluated information is not yet intelligence.

prompt: Which statement describes the general objective of the PA SIGINT program?
options: Providing strategic intelligence to General Headquarters in support of national defense policy
Maintaining effective Army-wide HF/VHF/UHF intercept operation and RDF capability
Providing real time intelligence to infantry brigades and battalions for AFP missions
Setting up an Army-wide secured intelligence communication network
explanation: Slide 10 gives the general objective; the other two choices are specific objectives on slide 11.

prompt: Which statement about cryptanalysis and traffic analysis in SIGINT is supported by the lesson?
options: Cryptanalysis re-integrates information, while traffic analysis deciphers messages
Both are used only on signals not directly used in communication
Cryptanalysis deciphers messages, while traffic analysis re-integrates information
Both replace the need to intercept the signals first
explanation: Slide 13 says that, as sensitive information is often encrypted, SIGINT uses cryptanalysis to decipher messages and traffic analysis to re-integrate information.

prompt: Which of the following is NOT one of the activities from which intelligence results?
options: Collection of all information
Dissemination of information
Evaluation of all information
Integration of all information
explanation: Slide 12 names collection, evaluation, analysis and integration in the definition of intelligence. Dissemination is a step of the SIGINT cycle on slide 22.

prompt: Which of the following is NOT a capability listed for ELINT?
options: Direction finding to a target in signals intercept
Voice interception
Jamming
Communication intercept through traffic analysis of electronic emissions
explanation: Slide 14 lists direction finding, jamming and traffic analysis of electronic emissions for ELINT. Voice interception belongs to COMINT on slide 15.

prompt: Which list contains the four things COMINT is capable of revealing?
options: Who is transmitting, jamming, text interception, voice interception
Location, direction finding, traffic analysis, voice interception
Who is transmitting, location, text interception, voice interception
Who is transmitting, location, cryptanalysis, text interception of traffic
explanation: Slide 15 lists who is transmitting, location, text interception and voice interception. Jamming, direction finding and traffic analysis appear under ELINT on slide 14.

prompt: Which statement distinguishes ELINT from COMINT?
options: ELINT deals with messages or voice information, while COMINT uses electronic sensors and surveillance systems
ELINT uses electronic sensors and surveillance systems, while COMINT deals with messages or voice information
ELINT is limited to jamming operations, while COMINT is limited to cryptanalysis of messages
ELINT is gathered from human contacts, while COMINT is gathered from intercepted signals
explanation: Slide 14 describes ELINT as using electronic sensors and surveillance systems; slide 15 describes COMINT as dealing with messages or voice information.

prompt: A SIGINT report must be checked against other intelligence disciplines before it is relied upon. Which disadvantage does this describe?
options: It cannot be clarified from the source
It sometimes cannot stand alone without substantiation
Enemy deception becomes possible if security is compromised
It cannot decipher encrypted messages
explanation: Slide 20 lists three disadvantages; needing substantiation from other intelligence disciplines is the one stated as not standing alone.

prompt: Which statement correctly describes the radio direction finder (RDF) system?
options: It uses a transmitter and jamming unit to disrupt enemy activities and fix their exact locations
It uses a cipher unit and Doppler antenna to decipher enemy messages and identify their speakers
It uses a Doppler antenna and analysis software to produce finished intelligence for brigade commanders and battalion staffs
It uses a receiver, bearing processor and Doppler antenna to monitor enemy activities and locate estimated positions
explanation: Slide 17 describes the RDF system as used for radio communication transmission countermeasures to monitor enemy activities and locate their estimated locations.

prompt: Direction finding to a target in signals intercept is listed as a capability of which SIGINT category?
options: COMINT
Both COMINT and ELINT
Neither; it belongs to cryptanalysis
ELINT
explanation: Slide 14 lists direction finding to a target in signals intercept under ELINT. COMINT on slide 15 lists who is transmitting, location, text and voice interception.

prompt: The second SIGINT function calls for advanced analysis of which information?
options: Intercepted communications signals information only, excluding electronic emissions
Intercepted communications and non-communications signals information
Encrypted communications and imagery information from the field
Decrypted human source reports from informants
explanation: Slide 23 states the function as conducting advanced analysis on intercepted communications and non-communications signals information.

prompt: How does the lesson describe the locations obtained through the RDF system?
options: Exact locations
Confirmed locations
Encrypted locations
Estimated locations
explanation: Slide 17 says the RDF system is used to monitor enemy activities and locate their estimated locations.

prompt: A SIGINT report is sound and well written, but it answers a question the commander did not ask. Which advantage is lacking?
options: Accurate
Timely
Relevant
Substantiated
explanation: Slide 19 lists accurate, timely and relevant as the advantages. A report that does not answer the decision at hand is not relevant.

prompt: Which description fits the Dissemination step of the SIGINT cycle?
options: Proper procedure of gathering information
Conversion of collected SIGINT data into intelligence
Timely production of intelligence to those who need to know only
Understanding the mission and direction needs to plan collection
explanation: Slide 22 describes Dissemination as the timely production of intelligence to those who need to know only.

prompt: Which description fits the Processing/Exploitation step of the SIGINT cycle?
options: Timely production of intelligence to those who need to know only
Converting collected SIGINT data into intelligence for planning
Gathering information by the proper collection procedure used by operators
Intercepted communication traffic and the estimated direction of the enemy
explanation: Slide 22 describes Processing/Exploitation as dealing with intercepted communication traffic and the estimated direction of the enemy.

prompt: Which list contains the three disadvantages of SIGINT?
options: Needs substantiation, cannot be clarified from the source, open to deception if security is compromised
Needs substantiation, cannot be clarified from the source, cannot be deciphered without cryptanalysis or traffic analysis
Not accurate, cannot be clarified from the source, open to deception if security is compromised
Needs substantiation, not timely, open to deception if security is compromised at any step
explanation: Slide 20 lists the three disadvantages as the need for substantiation, no clarification from the source, and enemy disinformation or deception if security is compromised.

prompt: Which of the following is a disadvantage of SIGINT?
options: It cannot be clarified from the source
It is not accurate
It is not timely
It is not relevant to tactical requirements
explanation: Slide 20 lists inability to clarify from the source as a disadvantage. Accurate, timely and relevant are advantages on slide 19.

prompt: Because SIGINT cannot be clarified from the source, what does this mean for the analyst?
options: The analyst cannot ask the originator of the intercepted signal what it meant
The analyst cannot decipher the encrypted traffic that was intercepted
The analyst cannot locate the transmitter by direction finding at all
The analyst cannot disseminate the result to the units that need it
explanation: Slide 20 states that SIGINT cannot be clarified from the source, so intercepted material cannot be explained by its originator.

prompt: Two summaries both trace back to one unverified report. Which statement is correct?
options: They count as one line of evidence, so independent support is still needed
They corroborate each other, so the claim is considered confirmed
They are accurate because both summaries were delivered in a timely and relevant way
They are relevant, so no further support is required for the briefing
explanation: The SIGINT reviewer says reports with the same origin do not independently corroborate a claim, and slide 20 says SIGINT may need substantiation from other disciplines.

prompt: Which statement about SIGINT security is supported by the lesson?
options: A compromised effort lets the enemy respond with disinformation or deception
A compromised effort affects only the Dissemination step of the cycle
Security matters only for ELINT operations, not for COMINT operations
Security matters only after intelligence has already been disseminated
explanation: Slide 20 warns that if security is compromised, the enemy can counter the government efforts with disinformation or deception.

prompt: To whom is intelligence disseminated in the SIGINT cycle?
options: All units in the Army-wide network
Infantry brigades and battalions only
Anyone using the secured network
Those who need to know only
explanation: Slide 22 describes Dissemination as the timely production of intelligence to those who need to know only.

prompt: Which specific objective of the PA SIGINT program concerns training of personnel?
options: To sustain efficiency through professional and technical development/training of PA/AFP SIGINT personnel
To continuously upgrade the SIGINT compartments responsive to the tactical requirements of operating units
To develop strategic monitoring sites in line with AFP external defense posture
To set up an Army-wide secured intelligence communication network for operating units
explanation: Slide 11 lists the training objective separately from upgrading compartments, developing monitoring sites and the secured network.

prompt: Which SIGINT cycle step directly follows Processing/Exploitation?
options: Collection
Analysis
Dissemination
Requirements
explanation: Slide 22 orders the cycle as Requirements, Collection, Processing/Exploitation, Analysis, Dissemination.

prompt: Which two steps are the first and last of the SIGINT cycle?
options: Requirements and Dissemination
Collection and Processing/Exploitation
Requirements and Analysis
Collection and Dissemination
explanation: Slide 22 begins the cycle with Requirements and ends it with Dissemination.

prompt: Which list gives the SIGINT cycle steps in the correct order?
options: Collection, Requirements, Processing/Exploitation, Analysis, Dissemination
Requirements, Collection, Analysis, Processing/Exploitation, Dissemination
Requirements, Processing/Exploitation, Collection, Analysis, Dissemination
Requirements, Collection, Processing/Exploitation, Analysis, Dissemination
explanation: Slide 22 gives the order Requirements, Collection, Processing/Exploitation, Analysis and Dissemination.
